# Chapter Twenty: The Breach at Glen Clova

The Grampian Mountains rose out of the pre-dawn mist like jagged, prehistoric teeth.

Glen Clova was a steep, narrow glacial valley carpeted in ancient Scots pine, blooming heather, and moss-slicked granite crags. At the far northern head of the glen, shrouded in dense morning fog, stood the ruined stone shell of Saint Jude's Monastery—a thirteenth-century Norman abbey whose roof had collapsed centuries ago, leaving only towering Gothic arches and crumbling perimeter walls.

Beneath the abbey ruins lay the natural subterranean caverns where Fiona's highland pack had lived in peaceful seclusion for generations. But tonight, the sanctuary was a trap.

Along the high southern ridge overlooking the abbey, three black, unmarked tactical command vans sat concealed beneath camouflage netting. In the center of the staging area stood a heavy six-wheeled transport rig, its flatbed carrying a pressurized industrial tank labeled with biohazard warnings. Four high-pressure dispersal compressors hummed with a low, menacing thrum, feeding thick reinforced hoses that snaked toward the valley below.

Around the perimeter, twenty heavily armed operatives of the Custodes Sanguinis stood guard, clad in matte-black urban assault armor, wearing full-face chemical respirators and carrying suppressed FN SCAR assault rifles equipped with thermal scopes and solid-silver ammunition.

Captain Thomas Mercer stood on the observation platform, binoculars raised to his eyes. Below in the abbey courtyard, his thermal imaging detected twenty-eight heat signatures huddled in the lower crypts—women, children, and elderly Lycans terrified by the gunfire that had erupted half an hour earlier.

Near the ruined nave, lying in a pool of dark blood, was the body of Martin. Brock had dragged his wounded coconspirator into the courtyard, attempting to trade the location of the pack's nursery for safe extraction, only for Mercer's snipers to drop Martin with three center-mass silver rounds the moment he stepped into the open.

Brock was currently pinned behind the altar in the ruins, snarling in agony, nursing a silver-shattered shoulder, realizing too late that Mercer had never intended to let any wolf leave the glen alive.

"Compressor pressure at ninety-five percent, Captain," Proctor Gregory reported from the command console. "Atmospheric humidity is eighty-two percent with a steady five-knot downdraft into the valley floor. Conditions are optimal for total aerosol saturation."

Mercer checked his tactical chronograph. 5:18 AM. "Begin the final countdown. Deploy Argentum-9 at 5:25. Once the dispersal begins, maintain perimeter overwatch. Any biological target that attempts to breach the ridge line is to be terminated with extreme prejudice."

"Understood, sir."

Six hundred yards down the ridge, concealed beneath the dense boughs of a centuries-old pine, Victor crouched in the damp heather, surveying the enemy layout.

Beside him were Alfonso, Marcus, Rebecca, and Father Edgar, who had refused to stay behind, his Franchi shotgun loaded with non-lethal heavy stun rounds and flash-slugs. Behind them, five fierce Scottish warriors from Fiona's perimeter guard crouched in half-shifted form, their amber eyes burning with desperate, protective fury.

"*Bakhzataa*," Victor whispered.

The thermal overlay bloomed across his vision. Victor traced the defensive perimeter: "Four snipers on the high rocks above the trail. Six operatives guarding the compressor rig. Ten patrolmen sweeping the courtyard perimeter. The compressor is powered by a central distribution manifold mounted directly behind the main cab."

"If Mercer hits that release valve, the gas will reach the crypts in ninety seconds," Alfonso warned in a low, gravelly rasp. "The children are down there. They won't stand a chance."

"Then we take the compressor first," Victor said, his tactical instincts taking complete command. "Alfonso, you and Marcus take Fiona's fighters and flank the high snipers on the ridge. Clear the elevated fire before they can pin us down. Rebecca, you take the lower drainage culvert—slip into the crypts, get between the gas line and the nursery, and prepare to evacuate the families into the northern pass."

"And what about you, lad?" Edgar asked, racking the slide of his Franchi.

Victor reached over his shoulder and drew *Lobera*. The celestial iron slid from the scabbard with a sound like pure chime, the gold Latin script glowing with steady, resolute sapphire fire. In his left hand, the Jamestown dagger caught the morning light.

"Edgar and I are hitting the compressor rig head-on," Victor said. "I'm going to take Mercer's toy apart."

Alfonso looked at the young man standing before him. For a fleeting second, he didn't see an American park ranger; he saw King Ferdinand III standing on the battlements of Seville, commanding his knights with absolute, unyielding moral clarity. Alfonso placed a heavy hand on Victor's shoulder.

"May the blood of Castile guide your hand, Victor," Alfonso said solemnly. "Execute the breach!"

The attack began with the fury of a mountain tempest.

High on the rocky ledges, the morning mist erupted as two massive wolves—Alfonso and Marcus—burst from the tree line like battering rams. The first sniper barely had time to shout into his comms before Alfonso's colossal black frame slammed into him, disarming the rifle and sending the operative tumbling harmlessly into a gorse thicket. Fiona's Scottish warriors swarmed the remaining elevated posts, neutralizing the snipers with brutal, efficient hand-to-hand takedowns.

"Breach! Perimeter breach on the south ridge!" an operative shouted over the tactical radio.

On the main access road, Edgar stepped out from behind a granite boulder and fired three rapid flash-slugs directly into the center of the mercenary compound. *BANG! CRACK! BANG!*

Blinding white magnesium flares erupted in the courtyard, instantly washing out the mercenaries' night-vision optics and thermal scopes. Shouts of confusion and pain echoed through the mist as operatives stumbled, disoriented by the blinding light.

Through the smoke and glare, Victor charged.

Two armored mercenaries spun toward him, raising their SCAR assault rifles and opening fire on full automatic. In the past, mortal reflexes would have resulted in instant death. But Victor, guided by *Lobera*'s preternatural resonance, channeled the Aramaic word *Malka*.

He swung *Lobera* in a sweeping figure-eight. A shimmering, kinetic distortion field snapped into existence around the blade, deflecting the high-velocity silver rounds into the dirt with loud, ricocheting metallic cracks. Closing the gap in two blinding strides, Victor pivoted, striking the first operative with the flat of his blade, shattering his rifle and knocking him unconscious, while his left elbow drove into the second mercenary's respirator, sending him sprawling into the brush.

"Mercer!" Victor's voice roared across the plateau, carrying the thunderous authority of an anointed sovereign. "Stand down! The hunt is over!"

---
